holidays.name: National Baked Alaska Day
holidays.description: A salute to the dramatic dessert of cake and ice cream wrapped in toasted meringue. It's the one dessert that goes into a hot oven and still comes out with frozen ice cream in the middle. Celebrate by making one, or by ordering one and watching it arrive with flair.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It honors a dessert linked to the 1867 U.S. purchase of Alaska, and the name is often credited to Delmonico's restaurant in New York.
holidays.funFact: The meringue works as insulation. The air trapped in it keeps heat from reaching the ice cream, so the dessert can bake briefly without melting.

holidays.name: National Dark Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day for people who like their chocolate bold, bittersweet and a bit sophisticated. Break off a square, pair it with coffee or red wine, and call it self-care.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It falls at the start of February, which is Celebration of Chocolate Month.
holidays.funFact: Cacao beans were once used as currency by the Aztecs and the Maya, so dark chocolate has a long history as something valuable.

holidays.name: Change Your Password Day
holidays.description: An annual nudge to retire 'password123' and the pet's name you've used since 2009. Treat it as a spring cleaning for your digital life, and consider a password manager while you're at it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, apparently created to encourage better online security habits at the start of the year.
holidays.funFact: Long passphrases made of several random words are generally harder to crack than short, complicated strings of symbols, and they're easier to remember.
